text: dsh-persona-switch 是供 DeepSeek Harness 使用的人设切换插件，可在运行中的会话里更换系统提示词。它注册动态提示词段、/persona 命令和 persona_switch 工具，支持查看人设列表、切换人设、关闭覆盖、重载目录，并设置人设是否替换完整系统提示。人设以 Markdown 文件存放在 DSH_HOME/personas，首次运行会复制随包示例，状态保存在本地。适合需要快速调整 DSH agent 行为设定的用户，不需要额外密钥或外部服务。

dsh-persona-switch changes the system-prompt persona in a running DeepSeek Harness session. It adds a live prompt section, a /persona command, and a persona_switch tool. Users can select Markdown personas, reload the directory, or turn the override off.
想在 DSH 运行时切换系统提示词人设。
怎么让同一个 DSH 配置支持多个可选 persona？
我希望不用重启就能更换 agent 的人设。
能不能把自己的 Markdown 人设加进 DSH 并重新加载？
I want to switch my DSH agent persona without restarting the session.
How can I load and select custom Markdown system personas in DSH?
dsh-persona-switch 的功能「切换系统提示词人设」：在 /persona 命令或 persona_switch 工具中指定人设名，即可激活对应的 Markdown 内容，并在下一轮提示词组装时生效。
dsh-persona-switch 的功能「管理本地人设」：用 /persona 查看列表、reload 重新扫描 DSH_HOME/personas 中的 Markdown 文件，或用 off 停止覆盖系统提示词。
dsh-persona-switch 的功能「选择提示词合并方式」：用 /persona complete on、off 或 auto 控制人设是否作为完整系统提示词；默认遵循该人设文件的 complete 元数据。
dsh-persona-switch 使用前须知：人设文件、当前选择状态和诊断日志保存在 DSH_HOME 下；首次运行会把随包人设复制到该目录。
我想在 TUI 和 Web 里用同一套自定义人设。
Can I turn off a persona override and return to the default DSH prompt?

dsh-persona-switch README · dsh-persona-switch：Live persona switching for **DeepSeek Harness** (`dsh`). Switch the system-prompt
persona from inside a running session — TUI, Web UI, or headless — with no
restart and no core patch. Ships with the switcher plus the example JB persona
(`jb`); a longer persona variant is deliberately not included and your own
personas live in `$DSH_HOME/personas/`.

dsh-persona-switch README · dsh-persona-switch：```
/persona              show the active persona + the roster
/persona list         same
/persona jb           switch  (name = personas/<name>.md)
/persona off          stop overriding the system prompt

Or just ask the agent — `persona_switch` is registered as a tool:

> jbに切り替えて

dsh-persona-switch README · Proof：Whether a persona actually overrides the prompt is measurable: point the route
at a local mock (`DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`) and read the request body DSH sends.
`test/capture-prompt.mjs` does exactly that, and the three states differ exactly
as the front-matter says:

dsh-persona-switch README · Proof：| persona | `complete` | agent-turn system message | harness identity |
|---|---|---|---|
| `off` | — | **2,823 B** | PRESENT |
| `jb` | `true` | **7,989 B** — byte-exact match with `personas/jb.md` | **absent** |
| `jb` | `false` | **10,814 B** (= 2,823 merged + 7,989 persona) | PRESENT |

25 tool schemas ride along in every case, `thinking` stays enabled, and the
session-title helper (a separate 363 B request) is untouched.

dsh-persona-switch README · Why a plugin is needed at all：DSH's own docs are explicit: *"Deployment-authored prompt text is config/
composition only … there is no end-user prompt-editing API."* The deployment
persona lives on the `dsh-system-prompt` row's config, and `dsh-persona` only
shadows it **inside one agent preset**. Neither is switchable while a session is
up.

This row registers one prompt section whose `text` is a **provider function**,
evaluated at every assembly:
section: Why a plugin is needed at all

text:
dsh-persona-switch README · Why a plugin is needed at all：```js
sp.section({
  name: 'persona-switch:persona',
  order: sp.getSectionOrder('DEPLOYMENT_PERSONA_PREFIX'),
  text: () => activeText(),      // ← read on every turn, not at boot

Switching disposes and re-registers that section, which emits
`system-prompt/change`; the next turn is assembled against the new persona.

dsh-persona-switch README · Install：**From npm** (one line per profile — each dsh profile is a separate install):

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web      add dsh-persona-switch
dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui  add dsh-persona-switch
dsh plugin --profile headless add dsh-persona-switch   # for scripting
```

dsh-persona-switch README · Install：Restart that profile (or just start it) and `/persona` is there. Nothing else to
configure — the package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` also
appends it to `dsh.profile.bundles` for you. Pin the version (`…add
dsh-persona-switch@0.1.2`) when a stale pnpm packument could hand you an older
release; plain `add dsh-persona-switch` resolves to `latest`.

**From a checkout** (development — a `file:` dependency is a symlink, so edits
take effect on the next `dsh` start, no reinstall):

dsh-persona-switch README · Install：```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add file:C:/path/to/dsh-persona-switch
```

**Desktop app (Electron).** Its `desktop` profile is *reserved*: `dsh plugin
--profile desktop …` refuses with `profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by
the Electron application`. Install it by hand (or run `scripts/install-desktop.ps1`,
which does exactly this and verifies the result):

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/install-desktop.ps1
```

dsh-persona-switch README · Install：then **quit the app completely (tray included) and start it again**. The `/`
menu now lists `persona`; `/persona <name>` runs host-side (no model turn, no
tokens). If an app update rewrites `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`,
re-run the script.

**Upgrade / uninstall**

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-persona-switch@0.1.2    # upgrade (pin: pnpm can serve a stale packument)
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-persona-switch        # uninstall
```

dsh-persona-switch README · Install：Uninstalling leaves `$DSH_HOME/personas/*.md` alone (your files, not the
package's).

dsh-persona-switch README · Personas：`$DSH_HOME/personas/*.md` — seeded from `personas/` on first run, then yours to
edit. The file stem is the persona name. Optional front-matter:

```markdown
---
title: JB core (persona slim2 / 8KB)   # shown by /persona list
complete: true                          # true = this becomes the ENTIRE system prompt
suffix: ""                              # optional text after first-party guidance

dsh-persona-switch README · Personas：| field | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | file stem | label in the roster |
| `complete` | `false` | `true` replaces the whole system prompt (harness identity, guidance, everything). `false` puts the text at the persona-prefix slot and keeps first-party guidance. |
| `suffix` | — | appended at the persona-suffix slot instead of the prefix |

Shipped seeds:

dsh-persona-switch README · Personas：| persona | size | complete | what it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jb` | ~8 KB | yes | the example JB persona |
| `terse` | 0.5 KB | no | example of a non-complete persona |
| `_selftest` | 0.3 KB | yes | answers only `BANANA` — proves the wiring |

`jb_full` (an 84 KB variant) is **not** in this repo and not in its history —
it was removed on 2026-10-12 and `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` keep it out.

dsh-persona-switch README · Personas：`complete: true` makes a persona the entire system prompt (see
[Proof](#proof)); `false` keeps first-party guidance and puts the persona at the
deployment-persona slot. Optional `suffix:` lands after first-party guidance.
Your own personas live in `$DSH_HOME/personas/` — drop a `.md` there and run
`/persona reload`.
dsh-persona-switch README · Adding your own：Drop a `.md` file in `$DSH_HOME/personas/`, then `/persona reload`. No restart.

dsh-persona-switch README · Files：```
$DSH_HOME/personas/              your personas (seeded once)
$DSH_HOME/persona-switch.json    { "active": "...", "complete": true|null }
$DSH_HOME/persona-switch.log     what registered, when, and why anything failed
```

State is deployment-wide (one `$DSH_HOME`), so a switch made in the TUI is the
persona the next `headless` run uses too. That is what makes scripted use easy:

dsh-persona-switch README · Files：```powershell
'{ "active": "jb" }' | Set-Content "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\persona-switch.json"
dsh headless "..."        # runs under jb
```

dsh-persona-switch README · Config：`cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: persona-switch
  name: dsh-persona-switch
  config:
    maxPersonaBytes: 400000   # truncate a longer persona (0 = no cap)

dsh-persona-switch README · Test：```powershell
npm test                                  # node test/unit.mjs — 30 assertions, no network
node test/capture-prompt.mjs --persona _selftest    # proves the system message
node test/capture-prompt.mjs --persona off          # and the stock prompt, for contrast
```

`test/unit.mjs` drives the real `apply()` against a fake Cordis context: seeding,
roster, switching, complete toggling, state persistence, the tool path, unknown
names, teardown.

dsh-persona-switch README · Test：`test/capture-prompt.mjs` starts a local mock that speaks Anthropic Messages and
OpenAI chat-completions, points `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL` at it, runs `dsh headless`
and reports the system message it received. Nothing reaches a real provider, so
it costs nothing to run. Set `DSH_CAPTURE_DIR=<dir>` to dump full request bodies.

The live path was verified the same way:

```
$ node test/capture-prompt.mjs --persona _selftest "What is 1+1?"

dsh-persona-switch README · Notes / limits：- **`complete: true` is heavy.** The persona is the entire system prompt every
  turn; an 84 KB persona costs those tokens on every request and can change
  prefix-cache behaviour. Watch it with `dsh-whale-widget` / `dsh-context`.
- Two complete sections would fail assembly — this row is the only one it
  registers, so keep other persona plugins out or switch them off.
- No client bundle: the switcher is a slash command + tool, not a Web settings
  panel. In the Web UI the command works from the composer.
- Nothing here is JB-specific — it is a persona switcher. The JB presets are
  just the seeds that were asked for.
- The DeepSeek route speaks Anthropic Messages (`POST /v1/messages`) with
  `thinking` enabled and `output_config.effort` set per model route; the
  plugin does not touch either.
- **Released**: the repo is public and the package is on npm (`npm view dsh-persona-switch
  version` for the current one). For the next release see [`PUBLISHING.md`](PUBLISHING.md) —
  §0 is the current state and §3 records the JB-seed call (made 2026-10-12, `jb.md` ships /
  `jb_full.md` never).
